opening.text: Imagine packing what you can carry into a cart. You leave your home, your farm, and the graves of people you love. You walk toward a place you have never seen. Thousands of Latter-day Saints did that. They are called the pioneers. They were ordinary families who trusted God with an extraordinary road.

mainMessage.text: The pioneers show us what faith looks like when it moves its feet. Their example helps us walk our own hard roads.

blocks.text: **They went out, not knowing** Abraham left his home without knowing where he was going. The pioneers walked the same kind of road.

By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went. By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Following the Pioneers” from the October 1997 general conference.
The foremost quality of our pioneers was faith.
Their feet moved because their faith did.
**Tried in all things** The journey was hard. The Lord told the Saints that trials would prepare them.
My people must be tried in all things, that they may be prepared to receive the glory that I have for them, even the glory of Zion; and he that will not bear chastisement is not worthy of my kingdom.

And now, I, Moroni, would speak somewhat concerning these things; I would show unto the world that faith is things which are hoped for and not seen; wherefore, dispute not because ye see not, for ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith.
President M. Russell Ballard, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Follow Jesus Christ with Footsteps of Faith” from the October 2022 general conference.
My great-grandparents followed Jesus Christ with footsteps of faith throughout each of their trials.
Trials did not turn them back.
**Singing on the road** The Lord told the pioneers to be glad and to pray when they were sad. Many sang as they walked.

If thou art merry, praise the Lord with singing, with music, with dancing, and with a prayer of praise and thanksgiving. If thou art sorrowful, call on the Lord thy God with supplication, that your souls may be joyful.
President M. Russell Ballard, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Follow Jesus Christ with Footsteps of Faith” from the October 2022 general conference.
I am grateful to them for never giving up.
A song can carry you a long way.
**Carrying each other** The pioneers did not cross alone. They carried each other's burdens.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “More Than a Hero” from the October 2023 general conference.
Ephraim Hanks will forever be a hero to those handcart pioneers.
He was a rescuer. Rescuers are heroes.
**Strength for the next mile** The Lord gave them strength to keep going. He still does.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
President M. Russell Ballard, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Follow Jesus Christ with Footsteps of Faith” from the October 2022 general conference.
He did it for the early pioneers, and He will do it now for each one of us.
The help He gave them is the help He gives us.
**Our turn to walk** We do not pull handcarts today. But each of us has a road to walk with faith.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Following the Pioneers” from the October 1997 general conference.
It is not enough to study or reenact the accomplishments of our pioneers.
We honor them by living with the same faith.

story.title: Nephi says yes

blocks.text: Nephi was asked to do a hard thing. He did not complain. He said yes.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
Nephi trusted that the Lord would prepare a way. The pioneers trusted this too. So can we.

My people must be tried in all things, that they may be prepared to receive the glory that I have for them, even the glory of Zion; and he that will not bear chastisement is not worthy of my kingdom.

And now, I, Moroni, would speak somewhat concerning these things; I would show unto the world that faith is things which are hoped for and not seen; wherefore, dispute not because ye see not, for ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “More Than a Hero” from the October 2023 general conference.
Ephraim Hanks will forever be a hero to those handcart pioneers.

**Renewed strength** The pioneers were tired. The Lord renewed them. He renews us too.
But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
President M. Russell Ballard, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Follow Jesus Christ with Footsteps of Faith” from the October 2022 general conference.
He did it for the early pioneers, and He will do it now for each one of us.
The same Lord is still at work.
**We run our own race** The pioneers are part of the cloud of witnesses. They cheer us on.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Following the Pioneers” from the October 1997 general conference.

Be the kind of person they would be proud to cheer for.

story.title: Through the sea on dry ground

blocks.text: Israel stood with the sea in front of them. Then the Lord opened a way.

And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided. And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
They had to take the first step before the way was clear. Many pioneers did the same.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

mainMessage.text: The pioneers show how many small acts of faith become something strong. They remind us that we belong to something bigger than ourselves.

By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went. If thou art merry, praise the Lord with singing, with music, with dancing, and with a prayer of praise and thanksgiving. If thou art sorrowful, call on the Lord thy God with supplication, that your souls may be joyful.
President M. Russell Ballard, Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Follow Jesus Christ with Footsteps of Faith” from the October 2022 general conference.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort, and to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God, and be numbered with those of the first resurrection, that ye may have eternal life—

But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

story.title: Manna in the wilderness

blocks.text: Israel was in the wilderness with no food. The Lord sent bread from heaven.

And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground. And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.
The Lord provided in a place that had nothing. Many pioneers told of the same kind of help in their own wilderness.

If thou art merry, praise the Lord with singing, with music, with dancing, and with a prayer of praise and thanksgiving. If thou art sorrowful, call on the Lord thy God with supplication, that your souls may be joyful.

**A hand on the trail** Some people stand at the hard places and help others across. Rescue is part of the path.

story.title: Be strong and of good courage
